title: Composition of the Additional Driver Charge on a Car Rental Agreement
content:
The additional driver charge on an agreement is the rate class's additional driver fee for each named driver beyond the free count carried by the rate class, taken for every booked rental day of the agreement, and the total is rounded to two decimal places.

**The quantities that enter it.** Three quantities and no others make up the charge on an agreement written on the Car Rental Rate Classes.

| Quantity | Where it is read from |
|---|---|
| The additional drivers named on the agreement beyond the free count the rate class carries | The rental record, against the free count published for the class booked |
| The booked rental days of the agreement | The rental record |
| The additional driver fee for each rental day | The amount published for the class booked |

**How they assemble.** The drivers named beyond the class's free count are multiplied by the booked rental days of the agreement, and that product is multiplied by the class's additional driver fee for each rental day. The money so arrived at is rounded to two decimal places, and that rounded figure is the charge.

**Worked through on hypothetical inputs.** Take an agreement, hypothetically, that books 4 rental days, names 3 additional drivers, and is written on a class whose published free count is 1 and whose published additional driver fee is 12 for each rental day. Two drivers are named beyond the free count. Two drivers multiplied by 4 booked rental days gives 8 driver-days; 8 driver-days multiplied by a fee of 12 for each rental day gives 96; rounded to two decimal places the charge is 96.00. Had the same agreement named only the single driver the class carries free, no driver would stand beyond the free count and the charge would be 0.00.
